issue: XM whole-tick intervals multiply an already rounded one-tick microsecond value.
matrix: Ten scores:eight timing failures,two exact-period controls. Independent controls at BPM100/125 have exact integer-microsecond ticks and identical intended row/event times. Actual tempo/speed changes are included.
observed: Score timelines lose10–72us in the authored cases;published audio/PCM ends1ms early. K03/EC3 at BPM150 cuts at sample2204 instead of2205 at44100Hz when a shared100ms presentation window isolates deadline rounding.
rejected_hypothesis: No frame-partition scheduler defect:current decoder already uses absolute PTS plus microsecond deadlines. The confirmed issue is rounding a single tick before scaling a multi-tick interval. No separate ID for the rejected hypothesis.

reference.scope: Precise BPM mode uses BPM/2.5 and carries fractional tick samples. Fvid documents the same ideal tempo law;the proposed fix stays within its existing microsecond clock and does not claim legacy-hardware FT2 timing or full sample-exact replay.

qualification: The fixed-window decoder test is explicitly separate from full-source duration/PCM and actual-worker gates,so the row-length error does not mask the subrow deadline error.
implementation: A private whole-tick-span conversion multiplies before division. Row durations and delayed Kxx/ECx deadlines share it;the public one-tick helper and packet timebase retain their existing signatures/units.
